newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine needs IMF fund to underpin hryvnia - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine needs IMF fund to underpin hryvnia - cenbank.

text.p: Ukraine needs a $1.5 billion stabilisation fund from the International Monetary Fund to underpin its new hryvnia currency more for political than financial reasons, according to the central bank chairman.
"Politically we need the fund," Viktor Yushchenko told Reuters late on Wednesday.

Ukraine's central bank says it holds enough reserves to maintain the hryvnia's current rate against other currencies. But officials have said Ukraine needs the fund to maintain psychological confidence in the new banknotes.
The hryvnia, unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange since its introduction on September 2, replaced the karbovanets.
An IMF mission is holding talks in Kiev this week on a three-year loan of $2.5 to $3 billion. But decisions on new credits will probably not be settled until the end of the year.
Missions have been visiting Ukraine each month to review economic progress and approve monthly disbursements under an $867 million stand-by programme approved in May.
